ratings_why.fun: Wiring a fuse and lighting it is a great mid-to-late puzzle, but the first three or four turns are still a trickle of +1/+1s.
ratings_why.distinct: Over a 7: counters that carry between turns and spill along the board's zigzag, with a real spend-now or hold-for-the-fight choice, is a growth shape no current tribe or BG tribe has.

verdict_why: Nothing is broken or unreadable now; the open questions (early pace, Piper burst) need playtests, not another rewrite.

points.text: The early curve is still flat: Taster Wendelin is a 1/3 that Blurts about every two turns. Letting its Blurt also give +1/+1 to one touching unit would give Tier 1 a real early fight.
After a Rat King chain every unit keeps 1 or 2 leftover Gossip, so Hearth Huddle pays the spend build too. The spend-or-hold choice softens late; fine if intended, worth knowing.
The Piper in Motley's loaded board can make seven attacks before the enemy acts. A fallback that keeps the fantasy: Blurt attacks start after both sides' Start of Combat effects.
Ilse versus Rat King order relies on Start of Turn going in reading order, which Part B only states for Start of Combat. Saying so on the card or in the rules would help the puzzle read.
Cold-Shed Tangle is the quietest Tier 4. Its Strays could arrive touching the Tangle so they always rejoin the wire, not just the nearest gap.

standouts.why: The Rat King makes one guaranteed full chain a turn; a capstone the whole board is built to reach.
The Bad Omen turns the mechanic on the enemy's board, and the enemy's gaps are its counterplay.
Little Fips jumps the news to the far end, so placement and gaps become a real puzzle.

weakest.why: Taster Wendelin is a weak body and a slow seed for the first turns.
Cold-Shed Tangle's 1/1 Strays are low output for Tier 4.
Ratskeller Landlady gives a gold back every three Refreshes; small for a Tier 2 economy slot.

flags.note: A fully loaded board's Start of Combat burst may decide fights before the other side acts.
Golden Thirty-Two with Bellringer under the King uses every text many times a turn; bounded per turn, not self-feeding, but a big high roll.
With the Rat King out, Wall-Runner's 5-Blurt Discover fires every turn.
